prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: concussion. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1280; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss came in from the policyholder's side after a sideswipe that happened while changing lanes. The insured reported the other vehicle drifted into their lane as they signaled to move over, and the claim was opened for bodily injury and property damage.

Entry 2: The driver is named on the policy and the coverage was in force at the time of loss. Nothing in the policy history suggests the vehicle damage predates the coverage start.

Entry 3: Claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact is being routed through the attorney's office. A letter of representation has been placed in the file.

Entry 4: Police report reviewed. Responding officers recorded the claimant as an occupant of the vehicle at the scene, and the report is consistent with the account given to us so far.

Entry 5: Photos of the vehicles were obtained from the insured and the other driver. The damage along the right side of the insured vehicle lines up with the described contact point, and the other vehicle's left-side damage is consistent with it.

Entry 6: Statements taken from two independent witnesses both describe the other vehicle moving into the adjacent lane during the lane change. Each witness account matches the others on sequence and position.

Entry 7: Claimant reported a concussion with headache, dizziness, and light sensitivity. The reported injury is plausible for a collision of this type, and no prior injury to the head or neck is known from the records requested so far.

Entry 8: The claimant has given the same account of the collision in each conversation, including the initial call, the recorded interview, and follow-up with counsel. Details of sequence and vehicle positions have not changed.

Entry 9: A few small scratches were noted on the insured vehicle's rear quarter panel in the photos. These may be older than this crash, and a separate estimate line is being prepared to address them.

Entry 10: Treatment records show a usual course of care, beginning with evaluation and followed by physical therapy and periodic checks. Symptoms have improved steadily and the frequency of visits has tapered as the claimant recovered.

Entry 11: Medical bills and wage documentation have been requested through counsel. Reserve has been reviewed against the treatment timeline and the current estimates for both vehicles.

Entry 12: File is pending receipt of the outstanding records and the final repair estimate. Next review is set for after counsel responds to the document request.
